analysis:
Examined all supplied ProviderLoop.swift BASE excerpts (lines 1–1192) and the complete bounded patch. HEAD adds selected-model recovery state, a test load override, saved enabled-model tracking and last-switch tracking (patch lines 719–730); initialization copies the configured enabledModels (HEAD patch line 882). These additions alone do not execute loads, alter authorization, expose prompts or keys, or change encryption/cache policy, so no concrete regression is supported here.
Relevant integration boundaries are TB-007/A-018 availability and memory admission, T-029 idle unloading, T-059 add-on holds, T-053 stale authorization, and T-041 cache isolation. Existing BASE state includes serialized load/reslice gates (410–481, 578–590), drain/add-on/update gates (482–505, 537–560), and verified artifact/cache identities (1006–1010). The new recovery driver must respect these controls rather than undo intentional unloads or load beside VMs, and preserve load-bound artifact/cache identities. Review ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery and changed policy-refresh/model-switch consumers together to establish eligibility, retry bounds, cancellation, no-eviction admission, and whether saved configuration is diagnostic only or serving authority. Their implementations are outside these supplied units; this is an integration coverage limit, not evidence of a missing control. No billing, attestation-proof or transport behavior changes are shown.
